dedupe_keys.name: minescan mine sites in wales natural resources wales

description: MINESCAN is a point dataset of metalliferous and non-metalliferous mine sites in Wales, digitised by Natural Resources Wales from the MINESCAN spreadsheet. The original four-year project began in 1996 for the former Countryside Council for Wales, carried out by John S. Mason for the National Museum and Galleries of Wales, and assessed the conservation value of over 1,000 old mines and mineralogical sites, ranking them against each other; it led to a network of SSSI and RIGS sites representing mineralisation in Wales. The layer is available through the DataMapWales view and download service and a WMS; it was created in June 2022 and published in June 2025. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): OGL-UK-3.0. Caveats: the survey is about conservation value, not safety or production, and reflects fieldwork from the late 1990s. For simulation it gives the locations of old mine sites across Wales, useful as an exposure layer for ground stability and mine water pollution in infrastructure corridors. Related catalogue records include BGS Mining Hazard (not including coal) and the Environment Agency discharges from abandoned metal mines.
